properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's ideas 4 and 6 in using_call.md (2026-10-01), for limitation 2: each `--call` is a terminal command VS Code prompts for, and "one regex cannot tell a read from a write".

THE IDEAS, in his words:
(4) "A short, approvable verb split by read vs write": `reflow2 read <tool> [json]` refuses any tool not annotated read_only_hint; `reflow2 write <tool> [json]` handles the rest. Both default `--graph-path ./.reflow2/graph` and quiet logging. Then `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` can safely approve `^reflow2 read ` and leave writes prompted.
(6) "Batch calls in one process": `--call-batch` reads JSONL of {tool, args}, runs them in order against one open store, and stops at the first refusal. One approval, one store open and one export for a capture burst.

WHAT IS CHEAP: (4) costs less than it looks. `--call` already decides read versus write from the served read_only_hint before it opens the store (main.rs ~757), so the split is a guard on an existing classification. (6) needs a JSONL loop around call_over_pipe and an all-or-stop rule.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS:
- (4) trusts the annotation. A tool wrongly annotated read-only would be auto-approved, so the annotation becomes security-relevant; a check that every read_only_hint is true would have to come with it.
- (6) puts several writes behind one human approval. For capture that is the point; for intent it must not carry a settle past the owner's word, which the store's signature check already refuses.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-01 — both: read/write verbs (step 3) and a batch door (step 6)
properties.no_relation_note: Searched "read only verb approve" and "batch calls one process". Nothing in the design addresses terminal approval prompts. The nearest is the door's own capability, which the field-report fact already hangs on, so it is cited in the text.
